## What the numbers say before any ranking

The interesting thing about this repo is that **severity and reach barely overlap**. The five `high`-severity God Functions (`postcssPlugin` 140L, `main` 153L, `setup` 126L, `getRollupConfig` 122L, `runEsbuild` 237L, `build` 293L) sit almost entirely in files with 0–1 direct importers. The files with real reach (`utils.ts` 18, `plugin.ts` 10, `log.ts` 9) mostly carry `low`/`medium` findings.

One file sits in both sets. That's where I'd start.

Also note the transitive numbers don't discriminate: `utils.ts` (29), `plugin.ts` (29), and `log.ts` (30) all saturate roughly the same ~30-of-52-file downstream cone. **Direct fan-in** is the useful signal here, not transitive.

## Triage order

| # | File | fan-in / fan-out | Why now |
|---|------|------------------|---------|
| 1 | `src/utils.ts` | **18** / 1 | Highest reach in the repo + God File + it's tested |
| 2 | `src/plugin.ts` | **10** / 3 | Only file that is both load-bearing *and* untested |
| 3 | `src/index.ts` | 4 / **17** | Fragility, not reach — 459L orchestrator |
| 4 | `src/esbuild/index.ts` | 1 / **11** | 237L function, but contained: one importer |
| — | everything else | — | Leave alone (see below) |

### 1. `src/utils.ts` — fan-in 18, fan-out 1

18 direct importers against a p95 cutoff of 9 and p99 of 10 — **double the p99**. It is simultaneously the God File (`crime_00047`, 424 lines, 1.4× threshold), so those 18 files are each coupled to a module none of them can hold in context.

The reason it goes first rather than second is that it's the *safe* one: `test_gap: 0` on every finding in this file. You can split it by responsibility and the existing tests tell you if you broke something. The two internal defects — `jsoncParse` swallowing errors into `{}` (`crime_00054`) and 7 sync I/O calls (`crime_00010`) — both propagate to all 18 importers, so fixing them here is 18 fixes.

Split by responsibility and update the 18 importers explicitly. Don't leave `utils.ts` as a re-export barrel; that keeps the coupling and just hides it.

### 2. `src/plugin.ts` — fan-in 10, fan-out 3

Fan-in 10 lands **exactly on the p99 cutoff** — top connectivity tier. It also holds `buildFinished` at 103 lines (`crime_00002`, 1.7× threshold), which carries the highest `agent_risk` of any God Function in the scan (0.54, above the 140L and 153L functions).

Why it's #2 and not #1: `test_gap: 0.75`. Ten importers depend on this and nothing verifies it. The extraction is cheap (`effort: small`), but the prerequisite isn't — you need characterization tests around `buildFinished` before touching it. That's real work `utils.ts` doesn't need, so `utils.ts` buys more risk reduction per hour.

### 3. `src/index.ts` — fan-in 4, fan-out 17

Fan-out 17 is the highest in the repo, well past the p99 of 11. But **fan-out is fragility, not blast radius** — this file depends on 17 things; only 4 depend on it (transitive 7). Restructuring it protects this file, not the codebase.

It earns #3 on internal mass: 459 lines (`crime_00072`) and three God Function findings — `build` 167–459, an anonymous 183–456, `mainTasks` 260–453. Those are **nested, not three separate problems**: one extraction pass on the `build` body resolves all three. `test_gap: 0`, so it's safe to do.

Caveat: this is the composition root. High fan-out is what a composition root is *for*. Extract helpers; do not invert dependencies to chase the fan-out number down.

### 4. `src/esbuild/index.ts` — fan-in 1, fan-out 11

Fan-out 11 hits the p99 cutoff, and `runEsbuild` is the worst single function by ratio (237 lines, **4.0×** threshold, `crime_00022`) with a 38-property options bag (`crime_00040`). But fan-in is 1 and direct importers is 1 — the entire refactor is contained behind one caller. `test_gap: 0`.

High value, low urgency. Do it when you're next in this file, not as a scheduled blast-radius reduction.

## Leave alone

**`src/log.ts` — fan-in 9, fan-out 0.** This is the clearest "don't touch" in the scan, and the most counterintuitive: it has the *highest* transitive reach (30) and 9 direct importers at the p95 cutoff. But fan-out 0 means it's a pure leaf, and its only finding is two unprefixed booleans (`onlyImportant`, `silent` — `crime_00019`, severity 0.30). Maximum reach, near-zero defect density. High fan-in is a reason to be careful, not a reason to refactor. Rename the booleans in place if you like; leave the module shape alone.

**`src/rollup.ts` — fan-in 0, fan-out 7.** `blast_radius: 0`, `blast_radius_transitive_importers: 0` — literally nothing imports it. It's the best illustration of why aggregate risk beats severity: it carries a `high` finding (`getRollupConfig`, 122 lines), a False Identity (`getRollupConfig` calls `setSilent`/`removeFiles` behind a read-shaped name), and a swallowed error in `runRollup`. All of it is confined to a leaf entry point. Real defects, zero ripple.

**`src/esbuild/postcss.ts` and `src/cli-main.ts`.** Both flagged `high` severity — 140L `postcssPlugin`, 153L `main` — and both effectively unreachable: `blast_radius` 0.14 (1 importer) and 0.04 (2 importers). Local cleanups whenever, never a blast-radius priority.

**`src/api-extractor.ts` — fan-in 1, fan-out 6.** Fan-out 6 is *exactly* the p95 cutoff, not past it. It's the marginal case that made the tier, with fan-in 1. Not a hotspot.

**`test/utils.ts` — fan-in 9, fan-out 0.** Nine importers, but all of them are tests. The unbounded `Promise.all` fan-out (`crime_00069`) is a genuine finding, just not a production blast-radius one.

## One thing to do before any of it

`crime_00011` — the repo ships no `AGENTS.md`, no `CLAUDE.md`, no skills, and `package.json` declares two bins agents have no way to discover. Effort is `small`. Every refactor above is an agent-assisted edit against files with 10–18 importers; writing the entry-point doc first is the cheapest thing on this list and it makes items 1–4 measurably safer.
